data.gender_notes: Maftuh is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root ‘af-tha-ha’, meaning ‘to open’ or ‘to clear’. In Islamic contexts, Maftuh refers to something that has been granted or made accessible, such as a door that has been opened or a passage that has been cleared. The name Maftuh carries the meaning “Opened, Cleared” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Maftuh usually hope their child will grow to embody opened, cleared and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is also used as a name for children born after a long and trying period, suggesting the idea of overcoming obstacles and finding new opportunities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Maftuh has deep spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. It represents the idea of opening oneself to the divine, whether through prayer, meditation, or the pursuit of knowledge. It can also symbolize the idea of overcoming obstacles and opening new doors to spiritual growth and understanding. In Sufi tradition, the name Maftuh is given to those who have achieved a state of spiritual opening and clarity, and who are able to transmit divine knowledge and wisdom to others. Ultimately, the name Maftuh reminds us of the importance of staying open and receptive to the divine, and of the role that transformation and growth play in our spiritual journey.
